insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (depends on Policy Schedule)

great.name: NCB
great.quote: “a sum equal to 50% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring Policy shall be provided as Cumulative Bonus irrespective of any claims… Cumulative Bonus can be accumulated upto 100% of Basic Sum Insured.”
great.reference: Section 1.A.III.4 – Cumulitive Bonus (page 22 as per TOC; exact page in extract shows the clause under 'III. my:health Active')
great.explanation: You get a 50% bonus on your base Sum Insured at renewal even if you made claims, up to 100% of the base amount. This means your coverage can increase over time without losing bonus due to claims.

good.name: PED Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED)… shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.”
good.reference: Section 1.B.I.i) Pre-existing Diseases: Code – Excl01 (page 26-27 area in extract)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded for 36 months from the start of coverage. This 3-year waiting period is within the normal market range and not a concern.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage…”
good.reference: Section 1.B.I.ii) Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period: Code – Excl02 (page 26-27 area in extract)
good.explanation: Certain listed illnesses and procedures are excluded for 24 months from policy start. This 2-year waiting period is standard in the industry.

good.name: Initial Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident…”
good.reference: Section 1.B.I.iii) 30-day waiting period: Code – Excl03 (page 27-29 area in extract)
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered during the first 30 days except accidents. This 30-day initial waiting period is typical for health policies.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization
good.quote: “We will pay for the Pre - Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred during the 60 days immediately before Hospitalization…”
good.reference: Section 1.A.I.4 Pre-Hospitalization cover (page 17 area in extract)
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days before hospital admission are covered. This duration meets the standard market practice.

good.name: Post-hospitalization
good.quote: “We will pay for the Post Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred upto180 days from the date Insured Person is discharged…”
good.reference: Section 1.A.I.5 Post-Hospitalization cover (page 17 area in extract)
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 180 days after discharge are covered. This is a good post-hospitalization coverage period.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: “Insured Person is eligible for Room Rent category of up to Single Standard AC Room. In case of admission to a room exceeding the aforesaid category, the reimbursement/payment of Room Rent charges including all Associated Medical Expenses… shall be effected in the same proportion…”
bad.reference: Section 1.A.I.1 Medical Expenses – Special Conditions (i) Room Rent & Proportionate deduction (page 16 area in extract)
bad.explanation: Room rent is capped at Single Standard AC Room and choosing a higher room triggers proportionate deductions, increasing your out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: “Procedure Sub-limits… Cataract per eye 75,000… Hernia Related 75,000… Hysterectomy 75,000… (and other listed procedures)”
bad.reference: Section 1.A.I.1 Medical Expenses – Special Conditions (ii) Procedure Sub-limits; Table I (page 16 area in extract)
bad.explanation: Fixed sub-limits on common procedures can reduce your claim payout if hospital costs exceed these caps.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: Not found in provided document extract.
bad.reference: Policy wording excerpt provided (no restore/reinstatement clause located; 'Sum Insured Rebound' appears only as an optional cover)
bad.explanation: Sum Insured is not replenished after a claim unless you opt for a separate optional cover, limiting your coverage for subsequent claims.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Non-Medical Expenses… are expenses other than those defined as Medical Expenses… Full list of Non -Medical expenses… (includes items like gloves, mask, nebulization kit etc.)” and “Optional Covers… 1. Non-Medical Expenses cover: We will pay for Non-Medical Expenses up to the limit mentioned…”
bad.reference: Def. 30 Non-Medical Expenses (page 11 area); Optional Cover 1 Non-Medical Expenses cover (page 23 area); Annexure I list includes “GLOVES”, “MASK”, “NEBULISATION KIT” etc.
bad.explanation: Consumables like gloves and masks are not covered by default and require an optional cover, meaning you may pay out-of-pocket for these items.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “Insured Person shall bear specified percentage of admissible Claim amount under each and every Claim, where Co-payment is applicable and as specified in the Schedule of Coverage…” and “On payment of Tier 2 premium… if Insured Person avails a treatment in Tier 1a or Tier1b cities, 20% Co-Payment shall be applicable on admissible claim amount.”
bad.reference: Section 1.B.II Specific: Co-payment (page 29 area in extract); Section C – Specific General Terms & Clauses: Premium Tier (page 68 area in extract)
bad.explanation: Co-payments can apply mandatorily, such as a 20% co-pay for treatments outside your premium tier zone, reducing your claim amount.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “Co-payment is applicable and as specified in the Schedule of Coverage in the Policy Schedule.”
bad.reference: Section 1.B.II Specific: Co-payment (page 29 area in extract)
bad.explanation: The exact co-pay percentage depends on your Policy Schedule, so check your schedule to know if co-pay applies and its rate.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: “The complete list of Network Providers… is available on Our website and can be obtained by contacting Us.”
unclear.reference: Section 1.C.3 Conditions for obtaining Cashless facility (page 34-35 area in extract)
unclear.explanation: The policy does not specify the number of network hospitals; you should verify the current network size and availability near you.

unclear.name: Built-in SI Buffer
unclear.quote: “IV. Optional Covers… These Covers are optional and applicable only if opted for… 9. Sum Insured Rebound… We will add to the Sum Insured, an amount equivalent to the Claim amount paid under Basic Sum Insured, subject to maximum of Basic Sum Insured…”
unclear.reference: Section 1.A.IV Optional Covers – 9. Sum Insured Rebound (page 24-25 area in extract)
unclear.explanation: An additional Sum Insured buffer is available only if you opt for this optional cover, and it is subject to limits specified in your policy schedule.
